newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut's Solidere up in week despite slide.
newsitem.headline: Beirut's Solidere up in week despite slide.

text.p: Solidere closed above last Friday's price on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday after sliding from two-year highs in mid-week trade.
Bank shares traded at record levels.
Both Solidere A and B shares rose to $12.875 from $12.5 last week. The shares soared during the week to their highest levels in two years to $13.75.

"I was expecting profit taking after the fast jump of the shares. I am positive on the share and think it will temporarily stabilise between $12 and $13," a broker who wished not to be identified told Reuters.

All three listed banks traded in strong demand. Banque Audi rose to $28.625 from $28.5 for a 90.8 percent rise since listing in January, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $21.5 from $20.75 and Bank of Beirut rose to $4.6875 from $4.5.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.73 percent to 185.34. The LISPI general index rose 1.28 percent to 95.19 and the BLOM general index rose 2.5 percent to 1101.67.

Market turnover was almost unchanged on the week at 1,875,813 shares from 1,858,225 shares for a value of $25,069,895 against $22,428,690. It was the biggest value of trade on the market since its opening in January 1996.
Solidere dominated the market with a turnover of 1,471,880 traded shares.
Last week's news that Solidere planned to open up share ownership to foreign investors in October fuelled the two-week surge by the company's shares.

"After the profit-taking period is over, I expect Solidere shares to move in accordance with the movement in the price of the company's global depositary receipts trading at $15.225 today in London," the broker said.
HSBC James Capel was optimistic about Solidere's prospects and said its clients were interested in investing in Lebanon's biggest company.

"We are waiting for the company to open up to foreigners. Meanwhile, we plan to be active on the GDRs here in London. We are quite bullish on Solidere," Albert Moumdjian, head of the Middle East and North Africa desk of HSBC, told Reuters in a telephone call from London.
"Being market makers as we intend means taking positions in the company and increasing liquidity on the stock," he added.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was flat at $1.28125. There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic, pipemaker Eternit or Ciments Blancs.
